question: A 28-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of pain in his left shoulder. He is physically active and plays baseball twice a week. The pain is reproduced when the shoulder is externally rotated against resistance. Injury of which of the following tendons is most likely in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Shoulder pain with external rotation against resistance" -> "Infraspinatus tendon involvement" -> 90% CHAIN: "Shoulder pain with external rotation against resistance" -> "Rotator cuff injury" -> "Infraspinatus tendon involvement" -> 85% CHAIN: "Shoulder pain with external rotation against resistance" -> "Common in baseball players" -> "Infraspinatus tendon involvement" -> 90%
enhanced_information: The 28-year-old man with shoulder pain on external rotation against resistance, likely has an infraspinatus tendon involvement. This is supported by the common occurrence of rotator cuff injuries in baseball players, aligning with the patient's activity. The evidence path mentioning inflammation and genes related to rotators does not directly impact the diagnosis in this case.
analysis: The patient's history of shoulder pain on external rotation against resistance, especially with his baseball activity, suggests a rotator cuff injury. Among the options, the most likely tendon involved in this patient is the infraspinatus, given its role in external rotation and its common involvement in rotator cuff injuries.
